extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of classical geometry; readers of Euclid's Elements
extracted.subtask_description: A sequence of Euclid's propositions (Book V) about 'given' ratios of magnitudes and how operations (addition, subtraction, composition, taking remainders, parallels, construction) preserve or produce given ratios. The page gives proposition statements together with proofs and corollaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. X
rubrics_metrics.description: IF two or more magnitudes have given ratios to one another, and if they have given ratios, though they be not the same, to some other magnitudes; these other magnitudes shall also have given ratios to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: Let A, B, C have given ratios to one another and given ratios (though not the same) to D, E, F. From given ratios of A to B and A to D we get D to B given, etc.; continued application of given ratios and composition/conversion shows D, E, F have given ratios to one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XI
rubrics_metrics.description: IF two magnitudes have each of them a given ratio to another magnitude, both of them together shall have a given ratio to that other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If AB and BC each have given ratio to D, then AC (their sum) has a given ratio to D. Proof uses that ratio of AB to BC is given and by composition ratio of AC to D is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the whole have to the whole a given ratio, and the parts have to the parts given, but not the same, ratios, every one of them, whole or part, shall have to every one a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let whole AB have a given ratio to whole CD and parts AE, EB have given (but not same) ratios to CF, FD. By constructing corresponding magnitudes and using conversion and previous propositions, one shows every one (whole or part) has a given ratio to every one.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF three proportional straight lines have a given ratio to the third, the first shall also have a given ratio to the second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let A, B, C be three proportional lines (A:B = B:C). If A:C has a given ratio, by finding proportional D, E and a third proportional F one shows F (and hence B) is given and therefore A:B is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIV
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a magnitude together with a given magnitude has a given ratio to another magnitude; the excess of this other magnitude above a given magnitude has a given ratio to the first magnitude; and conversely if the excess of a magnitude above a given magnitude has a given ratio to another magnitude, this other magnitude together with a given magnitude has a given ratio to the first magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two parts: (1) From AE (AB+BE) having given ratio to CD, construct BE:FD equal, show FD given and remainder CF has given ratio to AB. (2) Conversely similar construction shows CD together with FD has given ratio to AB.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XV
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a magnitude, together with that to which another magnitude has a given ratio, be given; the sum of this other, and that to which the first magnitude has a given ratio, is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let AB with BE (to which CD has given ratio) be given, and CD given together with that to which AB has a given ratio. Using proportional construction AE:FD etc., show CD together with FC (to which AB has given ratio) is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVI
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the excess of a magnitude above a given magnitude has a given ratio to another magnitude; the excess of both together above a given magnitude shall have to that other a given ratio: and if the excess of two magnitudes together above a given magnitude has to one of them a given ratio; either the excess of the other above a given magnitude has to that one a given ratio, or the other is given together with the magnitude to which that one has a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several cases treated: If DB (excess of AB above AD) has a given ratio to BC, then DC (excess of AC above AD) has given ratio to BC. If excess of AB+BC above a given magnitude relates to BC, then either DB has given ratio to BC or AB is given together with magnitude to which BC has given ratio, depending on comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the excess of a magnitude above a given magnitude has a given ratio to another magnitude; the excess of the same first magnitude above a given magnitude shall have a given ratio to both the magnitudes together. And if the excess of either of two magnitudes above a given magnitude has a given ratio to both magnitudes together: the excess of the same above a given magnitude shall have a given ratio to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By constructing equal ratios and using remainders and conversions, show that if EB has given ratio to BC then EB also has given ratio to AC; similarly treat the case where excess relates to whole together and deduce ratio to the other magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XVIII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF to each of two magnitudes, which have a given ratio to one another, a given magnitude be added; the whole shall either have a given ratio to one another, or the excess of one of them above a given magnitude shall have a given ratio to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let AB, CD have a given ratio and add BE to AB and DF to CD. If BE:DF matches AB:CD then AE:CF given. If not, compare BE:DF and AB:CD; construct BG such that BG:DF equals AB:CD and analyze whether AG (excess) has given ratio to CF.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XIX
rubrics_metrics.description: IF from each of two magnitudes, which have a given ratio to one another, a given magnitude be taken, the remainders shall either have a given ratio to one another, or the excess of one of them above a given magnitude, shall have a given ratio to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let AB, CD have given ratio and subtract AE, CF respectively. If AE:CF equals AB:CD then EB:FD given. If not, construct AG:CF equal to AB:CD and derive that GB (remainder) has given ratio to FD or similar depending on which ratio is greater.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XX
rubrics_metrics.description: IF to one of two magnitudes which have a given ratio to one another, a given magnitude be added, and from the other a given magnitude be taken; the excess of the sum above a given magnitude shall have a given ratio to the remainder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add EA to AB and take CF from CD. Construct AG:CF as AB:CD then show EG (sum) is given and GB (excess above given) has given ratio to FD (remainder).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXI
rubrics_metrics.description: IF two magnitudes have a given ratio to one another, if a given magnitude be added to one of them, and the other be taken from a given magnitude; the sum, together with the magnitude to which the remainder has a given ratio, is given: and the remainder is given together with the magnitude to which the sum has a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given AB:CD, add BE to AB and remove CD from given FD. Make GB:FD as AB:CD to obtain GA:FC given; since GE is given, AE+GA (sum together with the magnitude to which remainder has given ratio) is given; other part follows from previous propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF two magnitudes have a given ratio to one another, if from one of them a given magnitude be taken, and the other be taken from a given magnitude; each of the remainders is given, together with the magnitude to which the other remainder has a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given AB:CD, take AE from AB and take CD from given CF. Construct AG:CF similar to AB:CD to show AG given and hence remainders EG and BG etc. are given together with corresponding magnitudes; uses composition and prior results.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXIII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF from two given magnitudes there be taken magnitudes which have a given ratio to one another, the remainders shall either have a given ratio to one another, or the excess of one of them above a given magnitude shall have a given ratio to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From given AB, CD take AE, CF with AE:CF given. If AB:CD equals AE:CF then EB:FD given. Otherwise construct AG:CD as AE:CF and analyze remainders giving that EG (excess) has given ratio to FD or symmetric case.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXIV
rubrics_metrics.description: IF there be three magnitudes, the first of which has a given ratio to the second, and the excess of the second above a given magnitude has a given ratio to the third; the excess of the first above a given magnitude shall also have a given ratio to the third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given AB:CD and FD (excess of CD above given CF) has given ratio to E, construct AG:CF as AB:CD to get GB remainder with ratio to FD given and then composition gives ratio of GB to E is given, so excess of AB above AG has given ratio to E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollaries to PROP. XXIV
rubrics_metrics.description: Cor.1: If the first has a given ratio to the second and the excess of the first above a given magnitude has a given ratio to the third, then the excess of the second above a given magnitude has a given ratio to the third. Con.2: If the first has a given ratio to the second and the excess of the third above a given magnitude has a given ratio to the second, the same excess shall have a given ratio to the first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both corollaries follow by relabeling or applying previous proposition (9th datum referenced) to exchange roles of magnitudes and remainders.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXV
rubrics_metrics.description: IF there be three magnitudes, the excess of the first whereof above a given magnitude has a given ratio to the second; and the excess of the third above a given magnitude has a given ratio to the same second: the first shall either have a given ratio to the third, or the excess of one of them above a given magnitude shall have a given ratio to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given FB (excess of AB above AF) and GE (excess of DE above DG) each have given ratio to C, then FB:GE is given and adding given AF, DG shows AB, DE either have given ratio or the excess of one above a given magnitude has given ratio to the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXVI
rubrics_metrics.description: IF there be three magnitudes, the excesses of one of which above given magnitudes have given ratios to the other two magnitudes; these two shall either have a given ratio to one another, or the excess of one of them above a given magnitude shall have a given ratio to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let GD and KD be excesses of CD above given magnitudes with given ratios to AB and EF respectively. Construct corresponding HA, LE and use differences to show HB:LF is given; after taking given parts off remainders AB, EF either have given ratio or one excess above a given magnitude has given ratio to the other. Alternative demonstration uses adding given magnitudes to AB and DE to relate to C and uses prior propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXVII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF there be three magnitudes, the excess of the first of which above a given magnitude has a given ratio to the second; and the excess of the second above a given magnitude has also a given ratio to the third: the excess of the first above a given magnitude shall have a given ratio to the third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct GH:CF equal to GB:CD, deduce HB:FD has given ratio, and since FD:E has given ratio, HB:E is given; with AH given, HB (excess of AB above AG) has given ratio to E. Alternate case handled by reducing nested excesses and applying previous propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXVIII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF two lines given in position cut one another, the point or points in which they cut one another are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given two lines in position AB, CD that intersect at E; since positions are fixed and lines can be found, the intersection point(s) have fixed situation and are therefore given in position.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXIX
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the extremities of a straight line be given in position; the straight line is given in position and magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If endpoints A and B are given points, the unique straight line between them is determined and its magnitude is exhibited when drawn; hence the line is given in position and magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXX
rubrics_metrics.description: IF one of the extremities of a straight line given in position and magnitude be given; the other extremity shall also be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given point A and the straight line AC given in position and magnitude, take an equal straight line D to AC and cut off from AC a segment equal to D to find B; uniqueness of such point ensures B is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXI
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a straight line be drawn through a given point parallel to a straight line given in position; that straight line is given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through given point A draw line parallel to BC (given in position). Because only one such parallel can exist, its position is fixed and the drawn line is given in position.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a straight line be drawn to a given point in a straight line given in position, and makes a given angle with it; that straight line is given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given AB (line in position) and point C on it, draw line EC making a given angle with CB at C. Because the angle is given, set equal angle at D and construct EC accordingly; EC has fixed situation so is given in position. Note there are two possible such lines on one side that produce equal angles when extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXIII
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a straight line be drawn from a given point to a straight line given in position, and makes a given angle with it, that straight line is given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From given point A draw AD to straight line C given in position making given angle ADC. Construct through A a line parallel to BC; using parallel properties and equal angles reduce to Prop. XXXII to conclude AD is given in position.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXIV
rubrics_metrics.description: IF from a given point to a straight line given in position, a straight line be drawn which is given in magnitude; the same is also given in position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Proposition begins but full text/proof not included in this chunk; context indicates: given point and given-length segment to fixed line determine unique position up to symmetric possibilities, so the line is given in position.)
